ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The distance between the horizontal rails is $L = 1\,\mathrm{m}$, and the resistance of the rails is negligible. The mass of the conductor rod ab is $m = 1\,\mathrm{kg}$, and the resistance connected between the rails is $R_0 = 0.8\,\Omega$, with good contact with the rails. The electromotive force of the power source is $E = 10\,\mathrm{V}$, with an internal resistance $r = 0.2\,\Omega$, and a resistor $R = 4\,\Omega$. An external uniform magnetic field has a magnetic induction intensity $B = 3\,\mathrm{T}$, perpendicular to ab, with an angle $\alpha = 37^\circ$ to the plane of the rails. The coefficient of kinetic friction between ab and the rails is $\mu = 0.5$ (assuming the maximum static friction equals the sliding friction), and the friction of the pulley is negligible. The tension of the light rope on ab is in the horizontal direction, and the gravitational acceleration is $g = 10\,\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^2$. The rod ab is in a stationary state. It is known that $\sin37^\circ = 0.6$ and $\cos37^\circ = 0.8$.

1. The magnitude and direction of the current through ab;
2. The magnitude of the Ampere force on ab; do not add any other content.
3. The range of the gravitational force $G$ of the heavy object.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there are two horizontal guide rails; the thick black conducting rod ab on the right connects the upper and lower rails, with a at the upper end and b at the lower end; the power source on the left is labeled E,r, and forms a circuit with the upper and lower guide rails; a resistor R is connected in the lower branch; a horizontal light rope is connected to the right side of the conducting rod, and after the light rope passes around the pulley on the right, it suspends the heavy object G; the arrow of the magnetic field B in the figure is obliquely upward, and makes an angle α with the plane of the guide rails. Then reason: According to the polarity of the power source shown in the figure, the current in the circuit reaches the upper end a of the conducting rod through the upper rail, then flows along the conducting rod to the lower end b, and afterward returns to the power source through the lower rail and the resistor R, so the current direction in ab is from a to b. The resistance of the guide rails is neglected; the internal resistance r of the power source, the resistor R, and the resistance R0 of the conducting rod are connected in series, so I=E/(r+R+R0)=10/(0.2+4+0.8)=2 A. The magnetic field is perpendicular to ab, so the magnitude of the Ampere force is F=BIL=3×2×1=6 N. By the right-hand rule, the component of the Ampere force along the guide-rail direction is opposite to the direction of the rope tension, with magnitude F sin37°=6×0.6=3.6 N; the vertical component is upward, with magnitude F cos37°=6×0.8=4.8 N. Balance in the vertical direction gives N=mg-F cos37°=1×10-4.8=5.2 N, and the maximum static friction force is fmax=μN=0.5×5.2=2.6 N. In the horizontal direction, the rope tension T is equal to the gravity G of the suspended heavy object, and static friction can adjust within ±2.6 N; to balance the horizontal component of the 3.6 N magnetic force, the range of T is from 3.6-2.6 to 3.6+2.6, namely 1.0 N≤G≤6.2 N.
